memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "As he looked about and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother's son, he asked, 'Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?' And he said, 'God be gracious to you, my son.'" - Gen 43:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph's eyes fall on Benjamin — his only full brother, the other son of his beloved mother Rachel, whom he has not seen since Benjamin was a small child. His heart must have leaped. Yet still hiding his identity, he manages a tender blessing: "God be gracious to you, my son."

There is deep emotion pressed into these few words. Joseph longs to embrace his little brother, to reveal himself, to weep for joy — but the time is not yet right, so he pours his love into a quiet blessing instead: "God be gracious to you." Even while restraining himself, his heart overflows in a prayer of grace over Benjamin.

Notice what Joseph does with his overflowing love: he speaks a blessing. When our hearts are full toward someone — a child, a friend, a family member — one of the most beautiful things we can do is to bless them, to call God's grace down upon them. "God be gracious to you" is a wonderful thing to pray over the people we love.

Are there people your heart overflows toward? Learn to bless them, as Joseph blessed Benjamin — not just with warm feelings, but with spoken prayers that God would be gracious to them. Our words carry weight, and a heartfelt blessing spoken over someone can be a genuine gift. Let your love find expression in blessing those God has placed in your life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I express my love through spoken blessing over people?
2. Whom is my heart overflowing toward that I could bless?
3. How might "God be gracious to you" become a prayer I speak over others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to bless the people I love, calling Your grace down upon them. Let my full heart find expression in spoken prayers of blessing over my family and friends. Be gracious to them. Amen.
